title: MeridianCommerce - Eval & Quality Monitoring Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of Eval/Quality Monitoring: prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Discussed integration points for MeridianCommerce pipelines, data residency constraints, and proposed pilot with sample prompt sets and benchmark run.
topics: A/B comparison workflow and statistical tests
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) implications
Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
Benchmarking plan and trial next steps

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-28
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cruz (Redwood SE), Lina Chen (Redwood CSM); Rajesh Iyer (Meridian Head of AI), Marta Alvarez (PM), Tim O'Leary (SRE), Jing Wu (ML Eng)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samira, i'm the account lead here at Redwood. quick agenda: we'll run through the Eval / quality monitoring features in Console + Optimize, show prompt sets, regression alerts and an A slash B compare flow, then Q&A.

[00:18] Rajesh: great thanks. quick context, we're currently evaluating options for automated quality alerts across our product search assistant, we've got latency SLOs at 200ms p50 and strong cost targets.

[00:34] Ethan: cool. i'll start with a quick tour of how we capture prompt sets and label stores — there are two parts, the prompt set definition and the golden labels, that's what we use to compute regression stats. sometimes the transcription says 'kay vee cache' in logs but it's KV cache. apologies.

[00:55] Marta: just to be clear, we want the alerting to notify product when NLG quality drops beyond X percent on exact-match and also surface examples.

[01:10] Ethan: yep, you can set multi-metric alerts. we demo a composite alert: F1 drop + ROUGE-like score + manual sample ratio. the console shows the triggers, and we can wire to slack or pagerduty.

[01:30] Tim: question on data residency — our customer utterances cannot leave eu-west-1. can the evals run in-region or do we need private deployment?

[01:45] Samira: short answer: hosted can run in our eu region for most metadata, but for strict residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or a dedicated tenancy — that way logs and labeled data stay on-prem or in your VPC. we'll include the architecture diagram in the packet.

[02:05] Jing: how are A/B comparisons calculated? are you doing paired significance tests?

[02:17] Ethan: good question. our A/B compare supports paired tests where you can upload matched responses or run live side-by-side routing. we show confidence intervals, bootstrap tests, and a delta view. it's not just averages — you get per-prompt diffs and example-level annotations so reviewers can triage.

[02:40] Rajesh: do you keep the raw responses? retention policy? we have retention limits and need to be able to purge.

[02:52] Samira: retention is configurable per workspace — default 90 days; for Private you can set retention to match your policy. we also support audit logs and export for compliance.

[03:05] Marta: walk us through a real demo, please.

[03:12] Ethan: sure — pulling up the Console. first, i navigate to Eval -> Prompt Sets. here's a prompt set we created for a checkout flow: prompts, expected labels, and metadata tags. you can add stratified sampling rules to keep long tail cases.

[03:40] [Ethan shares screen; ambient typing sounds]

[03:52] Ethan: here's the label editor, teams can create golden labels or ingest CSVs from your labeling tool. note: labeling import sometimes maps 'true/false' as strings in the CSV which trips a schema check, you'll see an error inline.

[04:15] Marta: we use an internal tool for labels — will CSV import be fine?

[04:22] Ethan: yes, most teams use CSV import; we also have API endpoints to push labels programmatically.

[04:33] [05:00] Samira: on the integration side, our SDKs let you annotate requests with route IDs and metadata to tie invocations to prompt sets. that lets Optimize suggest batching and quantization per route later.

[05:20] Rajesh: i saw in the docs something called 'regression policy' — is that where we set thresholds?

[05:28] Ethan: exactly. policy has rules: sensitivity, required sample sizes, and auto-snooze. you can set a canary window to avoid flapping. for example we have a default that waits until 500 matched examples before firing a high-severity alert.

[05:50] Tim: will alerts include examples to hand to the model team?

[05:56] Ethan: yes. when an alert triggers we attach N examples where the delta is largest, plus the full JSON of input, model response, golden label and metrics. very helpful for triage.

[06:15] Rajesh: okay, cost tradeoffs — we run both a smaller opt model and a LLM for fallback. can we do automatic fallback if quality dips?

[06:26] Samira: you can route by policy — production routing supports tiers: low-cost base model with fallback to higher quality model or to a chat-based endpoint. Redwood Router can automatically switch based on health/latency and also on eval signals if you wire that.

[06:45] Marta: any support for prompt evolution — like AB comparing prompt variations?

[06:52] Ethan: yes. create a prompt-variant set and run AB compare; the UI shows side-by-side answer deltas and an experiment dashboard. you can promote a winning prompt to a route automatically or flag for manual review.

[07:10] [07:30] Samira: security quick note: we support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls, and optional KMS integration for key management. audits are available via the Console.

[07:46] Tim: KMS — can we bring our own key?

[07:51] Samira: yes BYOK is supported for Private; for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys in select regions. we'll add specifics in the compliance pack.

[08:05] Rajesh: competitors question — how's Redwood different from Anthropic or OpenAI on this?

[08:13] Ethan: Redwood's focus is production-grade serving plus integrated eval loops. Anthropic/OpenAI provide models and APIs but fewer built-in eval ops and rollouts; we combine serving, auto-batching, and eval observability so teams get cost/latency levers alongside quality monitoring.

[08:35] Marta: demo the regression alert timeline?

[08:40] Ethan: sure — here's a timeline view; you can click any alert, see the test statistics, and rewind to compare previous baselines. i'll create a test alert now — set sensitivity to medium, metric = exact match drop, window = 24h.

[09:05] [Ethan clicks through; indistinct mouse clicks]

[09:18] Ethan: alert created. now i'm going to run an A/B compare with a held-out prompt set. overhead: we can run server-side comparisons or run live traffic splitting. for benchmarking we'll run held-out then live split in the pilot.

[09:40] Rajesh: any automatic regression classification — false-positive filtering?

[09:47] Ethan: yes, there's an auto-triage classifier that filters noise; you can tune thresholds and label some alerts as 'expected drift' to reduce noise.

[10:00] Marta: timeline for pilot? we ideally want a 2-week pilot with measurable metrics.

[10:08] Samira: that's reasonable. typical pilot: 2 weeks, 10k-50k samples depending on traffic, we run latency/cost baselines, quality baselines, and an AB compare. we'll also do one security review for Private path.

[10:28] [10:45] Tim: for the pilot, we'll need a sandbox with EU data locality, and the ability to purge after the run.

[10:55] Ethan: will do — provisioning note: for hosted regional sandbox we can pin eu-west-1; for guarantees we'll offer a Private evaluation in your VPC if required.

[11:10] Rajesh: last question — do you support model quantization recommendations as part of Optimize?

[11:18] Ethan: yes. Optimize suggests quantization profiles based on latency/quality tradeoffs. we show expected token-level cost savings and a predicted quality delta so you can decide.

[11:35] Marta: lovely. that's helpful.

[11:40] Samira: okay quick recap: we'll send SOC2 and architecture doc, provision sandbox with eu region, Ethan will run baseline benchmarks, Marta will send prompt sets. can we agree to a pilot kickoff early next week?

[11:58] Rajesh: yes, early next week works. i'll sync internally and send calendar invite.

[12:08] [crosstalk]

[12:12] Samira: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the packet.

[12:20] Meeting end.
